Marc Randolph

Netflix Co-Founder, Bestselling Author, Entrepreneur, Mentor, and Investor

Marc Randolph is a veteran Silicon Valley entrepreneur, advisor, and investor. As co-founder and first CEO of Netflix, he laid much of the foundation for a service that has grown to over 300 million subscribers and fundamentally altered how the world experiences media.
Marc’s career as an entrepreneur spans five decades.

Most recently, Marc co-founded analytics software company Looker Data Sciences which was acquired by Google in 2019 for $2.6 billion. He currently sits on the boards of NOLS, the Truckee Donner Land Trust, and Cheeze Technologies.
Marc is the author of the internationally best-selling memoir, That Will Never Work: The Birth of Netflix and The Amazing Life of an Idea , which tells the previously untold story of Netflix. He is host of the top 10 Apple Podcast That Will Never Work , on which he works directly with entrepreneurs to provide 1-on-1 mentoring.
